course_description:
This course will allow students to build an intuitive understanding of the key financial concepts, tools and frameworks to better communicate with key stakeholders to further your career. Emphasis is placed on placing rigour in an impactful and practical context to analyse financial problems and devise solutions. Real world and real-time examples of events and developments are analysed and interwoven throughout the course to enhance skills relevant to managing financial problems in challenging environments.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

In response to previous student feedback, we have strengthened the connection between finance theory and practice by placing greater emphasis on applying concepts to real-world situations. Throughout the course, we draw on contemporary examples, industry insights, and case studies where relevant to help illustrate how these concepts are used in practice. We have also refined the assessment structure to reduce overlap between Assessment 1 and Assessment 2 and provide clearer distinctions between the objectives of each task. In addition, we have provided a more transparent assessment timeline, including clearer communication of key milestones and due dates, to assist students with planning and workload management throughout the semester.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with a set of mathematical, statistical and analytical tools that will enable them to value financial securities, construct portfolios of financial securities, and determine the price impact that a proposed corporate investment will have on shareholder value.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the key global influences and trends shaping the investment management industry.
Analyse problems to formulate and defend solutions, to achieve financial goals and objectives.
Apply core financial principles and investment management techniques to real world examples and experience.
Comprehend the principles of risk within the realm of finance to evaluate and recommend different strategies for mitigating these risks.
In teams, complete a portfolio analysis based on available financial data.

assessment_details.title: A1: Oral Presentation
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The oral presentation consists of a 5 minute presentation followed by 5 minutes of Q&A, which will be held in class. You will be assessed on your: (i) written memorandum (i.e., a summary of your financial analysis), (ii) ability to present your key findings, and (iii) ability to answer questions from the audiences. If you are unable to attend the oral presentation, you must contact the course coordinator. Otherwise, penalties will be applied accordingly. Further details about oral presentation will be discussed in class and posted to our course Blackboard site. assessment_details.other_conditions: Peer assessed. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: For this project, you will be in a team of 4 or 5 members. Your task will be to undertake security valuation and portfolio analysis. Peer Review: Group members are expected to contribute equally, fulfilling the tasks agreed on. If there are disagreements in relation to team members' contributions that cannot be resolved, students must bring the problem to the attention of their Course Coordinator as early as possible.
